title: Small-subdiagram criterion for an accessible full subcategory
statement: Fix a universe $\mathcal U$; small sets and diagrams are relative to $\mathcal U$, all Hom sets are small, and colimits have the universal property of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. An infinite cardinal $\eta$ is regular if a union of fewer than $\eta$ sets each of cardinality less than $\eta$ has cardinality less than $\eta$. A category is $\eta$-filtered if every diagram with fewer than $\eta$ morphisms admits a cocone. An object $P$ is $\eta$-presentable if $\operatorname{Hom}(P,-)$ preserves small $\eta$-filtered colimits. A category is locally $\eta$-presentable if it has all small colimits and is generated under small $\eta$-filtered colimits by a small family of $\eta$-presentable objects; locally presentable means locally $\eta$-presentable for some infinite regular $\eta$. For infinite regular cardinals $\sigma<\tau$, write $\sigma\ll\tau$ when $a^b<\tau$ for every cardinal $a<\tau$ and $b<\sigma$. Let $\mathcal A$ be a locally presentable ordinary category, let $\sigma$ be infinite regular, and let $\mathcal B\subseteq\mathcal A$ be a replete full subcategory closed under small $\sigma$-filtered colimits computed in $\mathcal A$. Replete means closed under isomorphism. The following conditions are equivalent. (i) There is a small set of objects of $\mathcal B$ generating $\mathcal B$ under small $\sigma$-filtered colimits computed in $\mathcal A$; no $\sigma$-presentability of these generators is required. (ii) For every sufficiently large infinite regular $\tau$ with $\sigma\ll\tau$, for every small $\tau$-filtered poset $I$ and diagram $X:I\to\mathcal A$ of $\tau$-presentable objects whose colimit $X_I$ belongs to $\mathcal B$, and every subset $S\subseteq I$ of cardinality less than $\tau$, there is a subset $J\subseteq I$ containing $S$, of cardinality less than $\tau$, which is $\sigma$-filtered in its inherited order and satisfies $X_J:=\operatorname{colim}_{j\in J}X_j\in\mathcal B$. Here sufficiently large means above a fixed small cardinal bound, independent of $I,X,S$. Moreover, whenever the approximation property in (ii) holds at a particular such $\tau$ and $\mathcal A$ is locally $\tau$-presentable, the objects of $\mathcal B$ that are $\tau$-presentable in $\mathcal A$ form, up to isomorphism, a small family generating $\mathcal B$ under small $\tau$-filtered colimits computed in $\mathcal A$.

source.place: HTT, Definition A.2.6.2, Definition A.2.6.3 and Proposition A.2.6.5, printed pp. 818-820 (PDF pp. 835-837, zero-based). The moreover clause is the conclusion of the first paragraph of the proof of A.2.6.5, with D = A^tau intersect B. Ordinary categories throughout this appendix. Read online, not locally archived. No Stacks tag states this accessibility criterion.

proof.text: Fix $\sigma\ll\tau$. If $T$ has cardinality $a<\tau$, its subsets of size less than $\sigma$ are covered by the images of all functions $b\to T$ for $b<\sigma$. Their number is at most $\sum_{b<\sigma}a^b<\tau$: each summand is less than $\tau$ by sharpness, there are fewer than $\tau$ summands, and $\tau$ is regular. Thus the entire poset $\mathcal P_{<\sigma}(T)$ is a cofinal family of the size required by [lem-coef-small-directed-superset]. That lemma gives a $\tau$-small $\sigma$-filtered superset of every $\tau$-small subset of any small $\sigma$-filtered poset. We will use this with either a $\sigma$-filtered or a $\tau$-filtered ambient poset; a $\tau$-filtered poset is $\sigma$-filtered by the definitions.

source.place: Definition A.2.6.3 and the small-subset construction preceding the proof of Proposition A.2.6.5.

proof.text: We record the colimit calculation needed below. Let $I$ be a small poset and let $\mathscr T$ be a nonempty directed family of subsets of $I$, ordered by inclusion, such that each finite subset of $I$ is contained in some member of $\mathscr T$. For $X:I\to\mathcal A$, put $X_J=\operatorname{colim}_{j\in J}X_j$. The transition maps $X_J\to X_{J'}$ for $J\subseteq J'$ come from the restricted cocones. A cocone from the $X_J$ to $Z$ is exactly a cocone from $X$ to $Z$: define the leg on $X_i$ using any $J$ containing $i$; two choices agree in a common larger member, and for $i\leq i'$ choose one member containing both to check the cocone relation. Conversely a cocone on $X$ induces compatible maps from every $X_J$. These operations are inverse. The universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] therefore identifies $\operatorname{colim}_{J\in\mathscr T}X_J$ with $\operatorname{colim}_I X$. All indexing collections are small since they are subsets of the power set of the small set $I$.

source.place: Proof of Proposition A.2.6.5, both small-subset reindexings, expanded by the cocone universal property.

proof.text: Suppose the approximation property holds at a fixed $\tau$ and $\mathcal A$ is locally $\tau$-presentable. By [lem-coef-ordinary-presentables-small], its $\tau$-presentable objects have a small set of isomorphism representatives; select the representatives that belong to $\mathcal B$, using repleteness. For any $X\in\mathcal B$, local $\tau$-presentability gives a small $\tau$-filtered presentation by $\tau$-presentable objects. Apply [lem-coef-cardinal-filtered-poset-reindex] to obtain such a presentation $X=\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}X_i$ over a small $\tau$-filtered poset. Let $\mathscr T$ consist of the subsets $J\subseteq I$ of size less than $\tau$ which are $\sigma$-filtered and satisfy $X_J\in\mathcal B$. The approximation hypothesis says every $\tau$-small subset of $I$ is contained in some $J\in\mathscr T$. In particular $\mathscr T$ is nonempty, and every family of fewer than $\tau$ of its members has an upper bound: its union is $\tau$-small by regularity, so apply approximation to that union. Thus $\mathscr T$ is $\tau$-filtered. Step 2 identifies its colimit with $X$. Each $J$ has fewer than $\tau$ arrows (a poset has at most $|J|^2$ arrows), so [lem-coef-ordinary-small-colimit-presentable] makes $X_J$ $\tau$-presentable in $\mathcal A$. Replacing these objects by their chosen representatives using the corresponding conjugated transition maps proves that the small family generates $\mathcal B$ under small $\tau$-filtered colimits in $\mathcal A$. This proves the moreover clause without needing approximation at any other rank.

source.place: Proposition A.2.6.5, first proof paragraph, printed p. 820 (PDF page 837).

proof.text: Assume (ii). Apply [lem-coef-accessible-functor-presentability-ranks] to the identity functor of $\mathcal A$ (it preserves all existing colimits), with any infinite regular lower rank. Its conclusion gives a regular $\rho$ and arbitrarily large permissible upper ranks sharply above any regular cardinal at least $\rho$. Choose such an upper rank $\tau$ sharply above a regular cardinal at least $\rho,\sigma$, and above the fixed bound in (ii). Then $\sigma\ll\tau$, the approximation property holds at $\tau$, and $\mathcal A$ is locally $\tau$-presentable. Step 3 yields a small generating family under $\tau$-filtered colimits. Every $\tau$-filtered diagram is also $\sigma$-filtered, so these very presentations establish (i). No assertion that the chosen generators are $\sigma$-presentable is used.

source.place: Proposition A.2.6.5, first proof paragraph; arbitrary large ranks as in Definition A.2.6.3 and Remark 5.4.2.13.

proof.text: Assume (i), and fix a small generating family $D\subseteq\mathcal B$. Choose an infinite regular $\eta$ and a small family of $\eta$-presentable generators for $\mathcal A$. For each $d\in D$, choose one small $\eta$-filtered presentation in these ambient generators. The union of the sets of morphisms of these indexing categories is small, since $D$ is small. Choose a small cardinal bound larger than its cardinality and than $\eta$. For every regular $\tau$ above this bound, every ambient $\eta$-presentable generator is $\tau$-presentable: a $\tau$-filtered category is $\eta$-filtered, so the defining Hom preservation applies. Each chosen presentation now has fewer than $\tau$ arrows; [lem-coef-ordinary-small-colimit-presentable] makes every $d\in D$ $\tau$-presentable. This is a single bound independent of the test diagram and subset. In what follows let $\tau$ be any regular cardinal above this bound with $\sigma\ll\tau$.

source.place: Proposition A.2.6.5, second proof paragraph: choosing tau so every generator is tau-compact; the uniform bound is expanded using small presentations.

proof.text: Let $X:I\to\mathcal A$ and $S\subseteq I$ satisfy the test in (ii), so $I$ is small and $\tau$-filtered, each $X_i$ is $\tau$-presentable, and $X_I\in\mathcal B$. Condition (i) presents $X_I$ as a small $\sigma$-filtered colimit of objects in $D$. By [lem-coef-cardinal-filtered-poset-reindex] take this presentation over a small $\sigma$-filtered poset $B$, with diagram $Y:B\to\mathcal A$. Let $Q$ be the poset of all $\tau$-small $\sigma$-filtered subsets $T\subseteq B$. Step 1 ensures every $\tau$-small subset of $B$ is contained in a member of $Q$; applying it to a union of fewer than $\tau$ members shows $Q$ is $\tau$-filtered. For $T\in Q$ put $Z_T=\operatorname{colim}_{b\in T}Y_b$. Closure of $\mathcal B$ under small $\sigma$-filtered colimits gives $Z_T\in\mathcal B$. Every $Y_b$ is $\tau$-presentable by step 5 and $T$ has fewer than $\tau$ arrows, so [lem-coef-ordinary-small-colimit-presentable] makes $Z_T$ $\tau$-presentable. Step 2 gives $\operatorname{colim}_Q Z\cong X_I$. Thus $X$ and $Z$ are two presentations satisfying every hypothesis of [lem-coef-presentable-presentation-comparison].

source.place: Proposition A.2.6.5, second proof paragraph: replace the sigma-filtered presentation by its poset of small sigma-filtered subdiagrams.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-presentable-presentation-comparison] to the $I$- and $Q$-presentations from step 6, with prescribed subsets $S\subseteq I$ and $\varnothing\subseteq Q$. It gives $J\subseteq I$ and $R\subseteq Q$, both of size less than $\tau$ and $\sigma$-filtered, with $S\subseteq J$ and $X_J\cong\operatorname{colim}_{T\in R}Z_T$. All $Z_T$ belong to $\mathcal B$, so its closure under small $\sigma$-filtered ambient colimits puts the right side in $\mathcal B$; repleteness then puts $X_J$ in $\mathcal B$. This proves the approximation property for every regular $\tau$ of step 5, uniformly in $I,X,S$, hence (ii). Together with steps 3 and 4 this proves the equivalence and the moreover clause.

source.place: Proposition A.2.6.5, second proof paragraph, applying Lemma A.2.6.6 and closure under sigma-filtered colimits.
